key_insight: An adversarial time-domain eddy-current example shows that gauge-penalized H¹ elements can converge to an incorrect state, while mixed H¹/H(Curl) elements provide reasonable results.
engineering_relevance: Electromagnetic finite-element predictions can remain unreliable despite mesh refinement if the approximation does not respect Maxwell’s differential structure.
method: Review H¹ and H(Curl) finite-element properties.
Construct a physically feasible, adversarial time-domain eddy-current problem in the a–φ formulation.
Compare gauge-penalized H¹ elements with gauge-free mixed scalar/edge H¹/H(Curl) elements.
evidence_signal: The reported numerical example shows persistent failure of penalized H¹ elements under mesh refinement, contrasted with reasonable mixed scalar/edge-element results.
watch_item: The abstract describes an intentionally adversarial example, not a quantitative benchmark of accuracy or computational cost across applications.
paper_title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
